plan_fields.label: Why Antares?
plan_fields.reason: Essay generated from the operator's about-me context

fields.expected: I want to work on software where the failure modes are physical and the system has to actually hold up outside a demo. Most of what I've built has pushed in that direction. At Summer Atlantic Capital I own the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection system, including the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, and a learning-to-rank layer for alert prioritization, because an anomaly system that floods analysts with alerts has created a second problem instead of solving the first. When I built a Playwright-based job-application agent, I designed it as a deterministic, operator-controlled system with fail-closed flags and an explicit validation ladder, since a capability that passes against a local fixture has not earned the claim that it works against reality. That instinct, deciding where automation should stop and what counts as evidence a system is safe to run, seems directly relevant to reactor hardware engineering. Antares is also the kind of place where the technology and the institutional argument are inseparable, which is what I spent the past year studying on my own. I would rather work on a nuclear system people will actually deploy than another speculative AI product.
